chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Whenever you love someone from your brothers, inform him of that; for indeed Ibrahim (peace be upon him)
said: 'My Lord, show me how You revive the dead.' He said: 'Do you not believe?' He said: 'Yes, but so that my heart may find reassurance.'

key_terms.إِخْوَانِكَ: Your brothers — here meaning fellow believers, spiritual brothers in faith
key_terms.لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي: 'So that my heart may find tranquility' — from Quran 2:260; used here as a model for the benefit of externally expressing internal states

ai.seo_question: Should a Muslim tell his brothers that he loves them?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches Nasr ibn Qabus that expressing love to one's believing brothers is a spiritual obligation, drawing an analogy to Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) request to witness the resurrection of the dead. Just as Ibrahim sought visual confirmation not from doubt but to achieve deeper certainty of the heart, so too does expressing love to a brother strengthen and make manifest what exists internally. The teaching emphasizes the importance of verbally affirming brotherly love in the Muslim community.
word_analysis: so that it may be reassured/find tranquility
